lawyer:
Dr Kamal Hossain with Md Shahidul Alam Chowdhury, Advocates -----For the Petitioner.
Hasan Ariff, Advocate -----For Respondent No.1. 
Rafique-ul-Huq with Md Shafiqul Islam, Advocates -----For Respondent No.2.
parties:
Bhawal Raj Estate Court of Wards ------ Petitioner
vs
Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
AM Mahmudur Rahman J: The petitioner, Bhawal Raj Estate Court of Wards, obtained Rule upon the respondents to show cause as to why the deed of release being 3092 dated 2-4-84 executed by respondent No. 1 in favour of one Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the respondent No. 1, RAJUK should not be directed to cancel the plan approved, if any, for construction of building over 13 acres excess unused acquired land and why respondent No. 1 be not directed to refrain from approving any plan for construction of house over the said land. 

 2. The land measuring 84.09 acres appertaining to CS plot No. 565 of CS Khatian No. 107 of Mouza Tejkunipara under Police Station Tejgaon at present Gulshan, District Dhaka was recorded in the names of Bhawal Raj Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others. Out of 84.09 acres of land 3.41 was settled with the tenants in 1925 and the rest 80.68 remained with the Court of Wards Estate of Bhawal Raj. Subsequently, the government acquired 18.47 acres out of 80.68 acres for Dhaka Improvement Trust (now RAJUK) for construction of Tejgaon-Gulshan Road under LA case No. 55.58-59 which was notified in the official gazette. The requiring body, the then DIT, took possession of the land on 27-6-1960. Petitioner, the Bhawal Raj Estate, states that for the acquisition no compensation was paid to it. It is further stated that out of the acquired area 13 acres unused land illegally was released in favour of the so-called owner Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others by the DIT contrary to the finding of the High Court in Second Appeal No. 685 of 1970 which on appeal was confirmed by the Supreme Court in Appeal No. 84 of 1974 and possession was handed over to them on 2-4-1984. The petitioner has stated that for creating false and fabricated documents regarding the land belonging to the Bhawal Raj Estate many cases in Civil Court were filed and Abdul Khaleque and others also filed case in the civil Court and ultimately it was settled at rest by the decision of the Appellate Division against this petitioner and others. Thereafter, the petitioner took the matter to the Ministry concerned and it is stated that the Chairman of RAJUK was given responsibility to consider the representation of the Court of Wards in respect of 13 acres unutilised land. The petitioner states that it is pending decision by the Chairman. 

 4. The Respondent 1 in essence stated that it was not aware about the settlement of the land measuring 3.41 acres and the management system of the Court of Wards. However, it admitted that out of 18.47 acres of acquired land only 5.47 acres were used by them for construction of Tejgaon-Gulshan Link Road. It further stated that RAJUK abandoned the unused 13.00 acres of land in favour of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others in lieu of Taka 15,75,000.00 (Taka fifteen lac and seventy-five thousand) as they were owners of the land as per document shown by them and on the basis of agreement made between RAJUK and Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others under section 92 of the Town Improvement Act, 1953. It is further stated that the agreement was made without any knowledge of the decision of Writ Petition No. 685 of 1970 and the decision of Civil Petition No. 84 of 1974. It is further stated that the matter is now under investigation of Bureau of Anti-Corruption who has seized the documents in this connection. And RAJUK was not aware about other cases and it was not made party in these cases. It is also stated that it approved the plan of respondent No. 2. 

 5. In a nutshell the respondent No. 2 states that the land in question was settled with the erstwhile tenant by the Court of Ward. Subsequently it was requisitioned and acquired by the DIT for the purpose of construction of Tejgaon-Gulshan Road. It further stated that out of the property acquired unutilised 13 acres of land was leased out by the RAJUK to Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others who having had been in possession transferred the land of Capital Property Ltd. who having had obtained the plan approved started construction thereon. It is also stated by the respondent No. 2 that the matter was ultimately sent before the Appellate Division and the Appellate Division by its judgment dated March 9, 1998 came to finding that the property belonged to Abdul Khaleque who subsequently transferred the same to Capital Property Ltd. It is further stated that the plaintiffs’ case (petitioners) was not accepted and all the Courts below correctly decided the matter. 

 8. Mr. Rafique-ul-Huq placed before us a decree passed in title suit No. 75 of 1967 and placing reliance on the judgment of the civil Court at pages 85 to 91 of the affidavit-in-opposition submits that the question of receiving compensation money has been settled by the decree of the Court against the present petitioner. On reference to the Affidavit-in-Opposition and the order of the Civil Court I do not find any substance in the contention of the petitioner as to his entitlement to compensation. Under section 101(1) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 it is the absolute right of the RAJUK to deal with the property acquired by them and in the present case they have sufficient authority on the strength of sub-section (1) of section 101 of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 to release the land to Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others as has been done under Annexure-B the deed of Agreement executed between the DIT and Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others. The petitioner has no right to challenge the transfer in question as it was released in favour of the owners. I am therefore, of the opinion that by the impugned order the respondent No.1 did not commit any illegality or infringed any of the fundamental rights of the petitioner. 

 In the result, the Rule is discharged but without any order as to costs. Consequently the injunction granted by this Court is also vacated.
